STEP 1 - Vessel type: flat plate, roughly square with rounded corners. No inner wall or shadow, so not a bowl.

STEP 2 - Vessel size:
a) Type: a square plate of this look is a medium dinner plate, about 22-25 cm across.
b) Reference: the bagel halves are about 10-11 cm across each. Two bagel halves plus the cucumber and cheese stick span most of the plate, roughly 2.2-2.4 bagel lengths across, giving about 23-25 cm.
Final width: 24 cm (square, area about 576 cm2).

STEP 3 - Food items:
- Bagel half 1 (left, with cream cheese): a half bagel about 10 cm x 8 cm, roughly 1.5-2 cm thick, mostly a base. Countable-style estimate: half of a 90 g bagel, about 45 g. Bagel is bread-like at 0.3 g/ml, but use the whole-bagel mass: about 45 g.
- Bagel half 2 (right, with cream cheese): similar size, about 40 g.
- Cream cheese: two dollops, each roughly 3-4 cm across and 1 cm thick, about 15 ml each, total about 30 ml x 1.0 = 30 g.
- Cucumber slices: about 6 thin rounds, roughly 1 cm thick, about 3-4 cm diameter. Volume about 15 ml x 0.6 = 9 g.
- Cheese stick (string or mozzarella-style): about 6 cm x 1.5 cm x 1.5 cm, roughly 13 ml x 1.0 = 13 g.

STEP 4 - Hidden food: no base layer visible beyond the bagel halves themselves.

STEP 5 - Energy per 100 g (as served):
- Bagel: about 250 kcal
- Cream cheese: about 340 kcal
- Cucumber: about 15 kcal
- Cheese stick (mozzarella-type): about 300 kcal

Totals: bagel 85 g, cream cheese 30 g, cucumber 9 g, cheese 13 g; total about 137 g.
